title: Toward Cognitively Grounded Machine Translation: The Morpho-Priming-Wait Model for Lexical Ambiguity in English-Arabic Neural Translation
abstract: Contemporary neural and large-language-model translation resolves lexical ambiguity implicitly: whatever disambiguation occurs is distributed across learned representations, with no stage at which a reading is chosen, recorded, or can be corrected. This position paper argues that ambiguity resolution should instead be an explicit, cognitively modelled, and inspectable stage of the translation pipeline, mirroring the sequence human comprehenders follow—detect that an item is uncertain, withhold commitment, let context pre-activate the licensed reading, and only then choose. We specify the Morpho-Priming-Wait (MPW) model, which couples three mechanisms drawn from human sentence processing. Connectionist morphology grounds lexical representation in Arabic root-and-pattern structure, keeping competing analyses of a written form distinguishable rather than resolving them in advance. Priming realizes spreading activation computationally, letting context raise the accessibility of the reading it licenses before a choice is made. A wait-and-see discipline defers commitment where either the output or the analysis is uncertain, revising it once further evidence accumulates. English-Arabic translation supplies unusually direct motivation, because Arabic orthography marks neither short vowels nor the boundary between a proclitic and its host: a user seeking either reading types the identical string بطاقة which may be the noun biţaqah 'card' or the preposition bi- together with the noun ţaqah 'capacity'. The system must therefore recover how many words it is reading before it can decide what they mean, a decision no sense inventory can express. We situate each mechanism against self-attention, sense-aware neural translation, and confidence-gated iterative decoding, locating MPW's contribution in their coupling and in the legibility of the decisions they reach. Because the proposal is theoretical, we close by specifying a disambiguation-accuracy benchmark, the ablations that would isolate each component, and the conditions under which the proposal should be rejected.

title: Exact Minimum Distance of a [[832,10]] Quantum LDPC Code: d = 15 by Exact Fold and Lift Enumeration
abstract: We determine the exact minimum distance of a two block quasi cyclic CSS code with 832 physical and 10 logical qubits. Earlier work had shown 10 ≤ d ≤ 15. We close the interval and prove d = 15. In each CSS sector the classical kernel has no nonzero word of weight 1 to 14 and exactly 416 words of weight 15, one orbit under cyclic shifts, all of them nontrivial logical operators. The proof uses the identity x^(2m) + 1 = (x^m + 1)^2 over GF(2). Since 416 = 13 · 2^5, the kernel folds down to a 26 bit code and lifts back exactly, so all low weight words can be enumerated level by level in about one second per sector. The paper gives the full proofs, the results, an 18 check validation suite, and the limits: this is a computer assisted proof, not a formally verified one. The code matrices and source files are not part of this record. They are held in a separate restricted record [restricted record link], and SHA256 digests in the paper pin every file.

title: A Differential Evolution-Enhanced Computational Optimization Framework for PID Tuning of Vehicle Cruise Control Systems Under Disturbance and Uncertainty
abstract: Simulation-based controller tuning for dynamic engineering systems requires computational optimization methods capable of maintaining search stability, solution consistency, and robust performance under uncertain operating conditions. In vehicle cruise control systems, accurate tuning of proportional–integral–derivative (PID) controllers remains challenging due to nonlinear dynamics, parameter variations, external disturbances, and changing operating conditions. Although metaheuristic optimization methods have been widely used for PID parameter tuning, their performance may be limited by an imbalanced exploration–exploitation trade-off, which can lead to premature convergence and inconsistent solution quality. To address these issues, this study proposes a hybrid centered collision optimizer with differential evolution, termed h-CCODE. The proposed framework incorporates differential evolution-based mutation and crossover mechanisms into the centered collision optimizer to enhance population diversity, convergence stability, and solution refinement while preserving the original collision-based search dynamics. The computational performance of h-CCODE is first evaluated using the CEC2022 benchmark suite, where the proposed method demonstrates improved convergence characteristics and competitive solution quality compared with the original optimizer and with four further metaheuristics. The method is then applied to simulation-based PID tuning of a vehicle cruise control system. Comparative results show that the h-CCODE-tuned PID controller provides a balanced transient response with reduced settling time and overshoot while maintaining a comparable rise time. Disturbance rejection, reference tracking, frequency-domain, and parameter uncertainty analyses further confirm the stable and consistent performance of the proposed control framework under non-ideal operating conditions. Overall, the results indicate that h-CCODE provides an effective computational optimization approach for simulation-based controller tuning in dynamic engineering systems.

title: RC-Attention Source Code
abstract: This dataset provides the source code used to train and evaluate the RC-Attention architecture described in the manuscript "A Lightweight Reservoir Computing Approach with Multi-Scale Attention for Robust Speaker Verification" (Silva, L. and Cataldo, E.), submitted to Pattern Recognition Letters. The RC-Attention architecture combines a temporal encoder with multi-scale, multi-head attention pooling to produce compact speaker embeddings for text-independent speaker verification. The code supports three interchangeable temporal encoders, corresponding to the ablation study reported in the paper: - a fixed, non-trainable Reservoir Computing (RC) layer (the proposed lightweight model); - a fully trainable Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU); - a fully trainable Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. The three configurations share an identical architecture, training procedure, and evaluation pipeline, differing only in the temporal encoder, so that they can be directly and fairly compared. The encoder is selected via a single configuration constant (ENCODER_TYPE) at the top of the script. Contents: RC_attMSP_Voxceleb1_clean.py — a single Python script that (i) extracts log-Mel spectrogram features from VoxCeleb1 audio, (ii) trains the RC-Attention model using the Additive Margin Softmax loss, (iii) reports closed-set diagnostics (retrieval accuracy, Equal Error Rate, t-SNE visualization), and (iv) profiles the computational efficiency of the trained model (trainable/total parameter count, GFLOPs per utterance via thop, and inference latency), matching the metrics reported in the paper's ablation and computational-efficiency tables. Data availability: This dataset contains source code only. The VoxCeleb1 audio corpus is not included and must be obtained separately from its official distributors (https://www.robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/data/voxceleb/), subject to their own terms of use. Software requirements: Python 3.x, PyTorch, librosa, soundfile, scikit-learn, pandas, matplotlib, and thop.

title: Joint optimization of detection, task allocation, and path planning for multi-agent cooperative interception under partial observability
abstract: Safety-critical autonomous systems often require multiple agents to detect, assign, and intercept non-cooperative mobile targets using only partial observations. These subtasks are tightly coupled because the same agents must balance spatial exploration for detection with goal-directed motion for interception, while target maneuvers remain uncertain. This study develops and validates an integrated multi-agent coordination framework for jointly optimizing distributed detection, dynamic task allocation, and path planning under partial observability. The problem is formulated as a coupled Dec-POMDP made computationally tractable through factored decentralized policies, parameter sharing, and centralized training with decentralized execution, and a Weighted Coordinated Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (W-MAPPO) framework is introduced to adaptively coordinate competing subtasks. W-MAPPO combines an observation-conditioned Policy Ratio Predictor, an LSTM-based history-aware processor for temporal modeling of target maneuvers, and a Voronoi-based collaborative detection module for spatial coverage coordination within a centralized-training decentralized-execution paradigm. Comprehensive simulation experiments across increasing target densities compare W-MAPPO with seven representative MARL baselines and two classical methods, supported by statistical testing, ablation studies, sensitivity analysis, and representative case studies. W-MAPPO achieves a 94% success rate in the 5 vs 5 scenario and maintains stable interception performance as the number of targets increases to 10 and 15. These results demonstrate the technical reliability and practical potential of integrated subtask coordination for partially observable multi-agent systems.

title: Plan or Retrieve First? A Scale Study of Tool Discovery Architectures
abstract: Tool-augmented LLM agents discover relevant APIs from large registries before planning execution, yet finite context windows prohibit injecting all tool definitions into a single prompt. The dominant approach, which we term Retrieve-then-Plan (RtP), embeds the user query and retrieves similar tools via approximate nearest-neighbor search. We study an alternative Plan-then-Retrieve (PtR) paradigm in which the LLM first generates Abstract Tool Stubs (hypothesized function signatures describing needed capabilities) which then serve as retrieval queries against the registry. title: Acting Through Registers
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) use generative visual representations to condition robot actions, yet how these representations organize action-relevant information remains poorly understood. We identify persistent high-norm spatial outliers in WAM representations and find that their action relevance persists even after normalization and K/V projection attenuate their extreme magnitude. Motivated by this observation, we introduce RegisterWAM, which adds learnable non-spatial registers to the world model and uses them directly for action conditioning. Registers alone do not fully eliminate spatial outliers; pairing them with observation flow-matching (FM) loss supervision suppresses spatial outliers while concentrating high-norm responses in registers. Beyond this reorganization, observation FM loss supervision also improves action learning without registers, motivating an additional noised-observation FM objective that learns current-scene recovery from corrupted inputs. The resulting model achieves 81.64\% success on LIBERO-Plus without additional embodied pretraining data or foundation models, reaches 93.0\% average success on RoboTwin 2.0, and improves real-world manipulation performance.

title: Towards Green AI: Evaluating Energy Efficiency for Quantized LLM Inference
abstract: While it is known that quantization of large language models (LLMs) reduces memory usage via lower-bit weights, studies quantifying the resulting impact on energy usage and carbon intensity are scarce. We present the first unified evaluation of weight-only quantization strategies for LLM inference across varying input/output lengths and GPUs, highlighting differences in energy efficiency in addition to accuracy degradation and runtime. We study quantized inference on Llama 2 7B, Phi 3.5 Mini Instruct, OLMo 1B, Qwen 2.5 7B, and Qwen 2.5 14B across GLUE MNLI, MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K datasets, evaluating 10 post-training quantization (PTQ) strategies on NVIDIA H100, A6000, A100, and L4 GPUs. We identify a novel trend showing that quantization techniques tend to exhibit peak energy efficiency relative to full-precision baselines when inputs are sufficiently long and outputs are short. Furthermore, we show that quantization strategies become marginally more energy-efficient relative to full-precision models as batch sizes increase, though gains are modest. Notably, fused-kernel implementations such as EETQ int8 and Bitsandbytes int8 offer the highest energy savings, up to 4x compared to FP32 on short text generation, with negligible accuracy loss. Finally, we observe that energy usage closely tracks runtime on our evaluated benchmarks, indicating that, in practice, latency optimization can serve as a reliable proxy for reducing the environmental footprint of LLM services. We conclude with suggested directions for strategically selecting low-carbon quantization strategies based on specific inference requirements.

title: Pan-cancer estimation of prognostic immune biomarkers from histopathology using artificial intelligence
abstract: Multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) assays such as ImmunoProfile provide standardized quantification of prognostic immune markers but are costly and not routinely used in clinical settings. We developed a weakly-supervised AI model, HistoProfile, to estimate intratumoral cell densities of key immune biomarkers (CD8, FOXP3, PD-1, and PD-L1) and the PD-L1 tumor proportion score from routine H&E-stained whole-slide images. Trained on a large pan-cancer cohort with paired H&E and mIF data, HistoProfile discriminated biomarker-high from biomarker-low tumors in held-out samples and tumor-specific subgroups (AUROCs of 0.78-0.89 across biomarkers). Critically, the estimated biomarkers preserved prognostic stratification in downstream survival analyses, and showed cancer-specific survival associations across TCGA cohorts where mIF is unavailable. These findings support scalable H&E-based estimation of key immune biomarker measurements for large-scale immune profiling and risk stratification.

title: Data and code for How Meteorological Data Choice Changes Solar and Wind Investment Decisions in Northern Nigeria
abstract: This dataset and code package supports a paired assessment of NASA POWER weather estimates and independent World Bank-financed West African Power Pool (WAPP) station measurements at Bauchi and Kano, Nigeria. It contains matched hourly solar irradiance, 10 m wind speed and temperature data for two measurement campaigns in 2021–2023; archived NASA POWER hourly responses; NASA monthly responses and resource summaries for 2001–2025; 15 numerical summary tables; detailed model outputs; Python scripts; and Figures 2–7 in PNG and PDF formats.The calculations propagate weather-source differences through a nominal 500 kWp fixed-tilt photovoltaic design and a 500 kW EWT DW54 turbine at an assumed 50 m hub height. Outputs include resource-validation errors, modeled production, conditional discounted LCOE, wind-shear and loss sensitivity, capital-cost and finance thresholds, paired-month resampling, and site and technology ranking reversals. The main workflow uses archived NASA responses by default.Nigerian project quotations have not been verified; LCOE and technology choices are conditional scenarios. The turbine power curve is approximately digitized from a manufacturer graphic, and hub-height wind is extrapolated. The historical NASA record describes modeled resource variation rather than additional independent station validation. Original minute-resolution WAPP observations are available through the source repository; this deposit contains hourly derivatives, processing code and input checksums. Third-party sources retain their attribution and reuse conditions.

title: Automating Injury Severity Score Calculation From Free-Text Discharge Diagnoses Using Domain-Specific Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models: Retrospective Validation Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Trauma registries are crucial for evaluating the prognosis of injuries and the quality of trauma care. However, the calculation of Injury Severity Score (ISS) remains a predominantly manual process, which is labor-intensive, potentially error-prone, and difficult to scale. Automating this process is a critical step toward enhancing the efficiency and quality of trauma registry data. OBJECTIVE: This study conducts a feasibility test on the use of large language models (LLMs) to automatically calculate ISS from free-text discharge diagnoses. We specifically investigate the efficacy of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to enhance LLM accuracy by incorporating knowledge from the Abbreviated Injury Scale. We compare the performance of baseline LLMs against models augmented with both a standard RAG and a novel, domain-specific RAG framework. METHODS: In this retrospective validation study, we used deidentified, free-text discharge diagnoses from trauma patients at Chang Gung Memorial Hospital (Linkou, Taiwan) in 2022. Against a physician-verified gold standard, we compared the performance of three systems: (1) baseline LLMs, (2) LLMs with standard RAG, and (3) LLMs with domain-specific RAG, for which the retriever was fine-tuned on trauma-related ICD-10 (International Statistical Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision) codes. Performance was evaluated on a physician-verified test set across exact ISS prediction, tolerance-based accuracy, and ISS severity categories. RESULTS: Baseline state-of-the-art LLMs achieve modest exact-match (EM) accuracy, ranging from 47.3% to 64.7%. Standard RAG did not produce consistent gains (54.3% to 60.3%), whereas the domain-specific RAG substantially improved accuracy (62.7% to 75.3%). Performance gains were most pronounced in patients with moderate to severe injuries. GPT-4.1 with domain-specific RAG reached the highest EM accuracy (75.3%, 95% CI 66.1%-82.7%), compared with 70.0% for the deterministic International Classification of Diseases and R statistical software (ICDPIC-R) baseline. Tolerance-based and categorical analyses confirm substantial gains with the domain-specific RAG framework in clinically relevant ranges. CONCLUSIONS: This single-center feasibility study suggests that LLMs augmented with a domain-specific retriever can calculate the ISS from free-text discharge diagnoses with overall accuracy comparable to that of a deterministic coding tool, with the advantage concentrated in the most severe injuries. This approach may help alleviate the administrative burden of manual coding, enhance standardization, and improve the quality of trauma registry data. Future multi-institutional validation is needed to confirm these findings.

title: Punching Down: Deflation Attacks on the Tor Network
abstract: Tor is an anonymity network with relays run by thousands of volunteers across the world. Load-balancing among these relays depends on bandwidth measurement carried out by directory authorities. Prior work has explored attacks in which the attacker prioritizes measurement traffic to cause an inflation of weights (i.e., the probability of being selected) assigned to malicious relays.

title: GenAI Multi‐agent Systems
abstract: This chapter examines how Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), transforms coordination capabilities in multi-agent systems (MAS) for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs). The chapter covers coordination mechanisms, communication protocols, distributed reasoning, and collaborative decision-making in CAV contexts. It examines how GenAI enables sophisticated coordination beyond classical symbolic approaches, supporting natural language communication, context sharing, and adaptive collaboration. Applications include multi-vehicle coordination, traffic management, and collaborative navigation. The chapter emphasizes how GenAI addresses the complexity of real-world traffic scenarios demanding sophisticated coordination that goes beyond traditional rule-based multi-agent systems.

title: Revisiting Generative vs. Dense Retrieval: A Static Value Prior Reverses the Gap
abstract: Generative retrieval (GR) has emerged as a strong candidate generator for sequential recommendation as language models and semantic-item identifiers have improved. However, GR is not a uniformly stronger replacement of dense retrieval (DR) in online retail candidate generation. We examine their differences on two Amazon Toys datasets under different metrics. GR leads on best relevant item value among users both methods cover, while DR leads on exact-target recall and relevant value across the ranked list. With deep analysis, we find that popularity contributes the most to GR's measured value lead. Adding the same static item value to DR in one reranking step reverses this lead and keeps recall above GR. Finally, on an industrial-scale internal e-commerce dataset with LLM-judged relevance, we show that a 14B SID-LLM still underperforms a $47\times$ smaller dense encoder.

title: LiFUSE: Frequency-Spatial Unified Self-Supervised Pretraining for Liver Disease Analysis on Non-contrast CT
abstract: Given the growing global burden of liver tumors and diffuse liver diseases, non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is increasingly used for opportunistic screening because of its low cost and favorable safety profile. However, downstream tasks such as tumor detection and fine-grained disease diagnosis remain challenging due to NCCT's inherently low tissue contrast, lack of hemodynamic enhancement, and complex anatomical background. These limitations make subtle, heterogeneous, and multifocal hepatic lesions difficult to identify. Although large-scale self-supervised pretraining can learn robust representations from unlabeled NCCT scans, conventional voxel-wise reconstruction does not fully exploit the complementary information available in NCCT. Under weak NCCT contrast, low-level intensity patterns become less informative for pathology recognition, limiting the capture of lesion-specific discriminative features. In this paper, we propose the Liver Frequency-Spatial Unified Self-Supervised Pretraining (LiFUSE). The frequency branch applies random band-stop masking and spectrum reconstruction to encourage the model to capture subtle differences between lesions and surrounding tissues, while the spatial branch performs hybrid-granularity masked volumetric reconstruction to accommodate lesions of diverse sizes and morphologies. Finally, a cross-domain consistency scheme couples the spatial and frequency branches, yielding more discriminative representations for hepatic structures and lesions. Extensive experiments on three clinically relevant tasks across internal cohorts and a public target-domain transfer setting show that LiFUSE consistently outperforms strong baselines. These results suggest that unified frequency-spatial learning can improve liver disease analysis on NCCT, highlighting its potential for large-scale screening.

title: Puncturing-inclusion constructions of optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes using semifield codes
abstract: Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes are essential components of the multilevel construction of constant dimension codes for random network coding. This paper aims to construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes, focusing on the diagram \([3,3,3,5]\) with rank distance \(3\). We construct an optimal \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) Ferrers diagram rank-metric code for every prime power \(q\), thereby answering an open problem posed by Etzion et al. in 2016~\cite{Etzion2016}. The construction first builds a \([3\times4,4,3]_q\) MRD code and then proves that the Delsarte dual of its puncturing on the last column contains a \([3\times3,3,3]_q\) MRD code, which comes from semifield codes. We further construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for two infinite families of Ferrers diagrams: the first relies on the \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) construction and holds for every prime power \(q\), while the second is binary and obtained directly by the puncturing-inclusion construction.

title: TwinPrune: Density-Aware Two-Phase Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models
abstract: We propose a unified spatial-density signal to score token importance for both inference phases: bipartite merge for prefill and KV eviction for decode, yielding measurable gains in each stage. To isolate the two phases, we split benchmarks by scoring logic. Prefill probes (MMBench, POPE, ScienceQA) evaluate only the first decoded token; their accuracy reflects prefill logits argmax before any decode KV eviction. Full-pipeline probes (TextVQA, DocVQA, MM-Vet) assess the complete generated sequence and capture both phases. We identify a critical evaluation pitfall: decode pruning claims validated solely on prefill probes measure prefill quality, not decode performance. Experiments show discarding all visual KV during decode barely affects prefill-probe accuracy but degrades TextVQA and MM-Vet drastically; this insensitivity stems from the scoring rule, not compression intensity. Evaluated on seven model variants (InternVL-3.5, Qwen3-VL, LLaVA-1.5) and three full-pipeline benchmarks, our method achieves a three-way Pareto frontier across compute, memory and accuracy. Density-based prefill compression maintains strong accuracy, scales linearly with visual token count, and delivers 100x faster token selection at high resolution. For decode, density top-k KV eviction consistently outperforms strong baselines H2O, SnapKV and StreamingLLM on TextVQA and MM-Vet across three retention ratios. At 0.125 keep ratio on TextVQA, it surpasses H2O by 9.6 points; InternVL-3.5 models (2B to 38B) maintain a 7 to 10 point advantage. Compression scales favorably with model size: every measured 8B to 38B model transition reduces accuracy loss instead of worsening it. We suggest MM-Vet or DocVQA as mandatory full-pipeline validation for any decode-phase claims. Our code is available at https://github.com/Kai-Liu001/TwinPrune

Experiments show discarding all visual KV during decode barely affects prefill-probe accuracy but degrades TextVQA and MM-Vet drastically; this insensitivity stems from the scoring rule, not compression intensity. Evaluated on seven model variants (InternVL-3.5, Qwen3-VL, LLaVA-1.5) and three full-pipeline benchmarks, our method achieves a three-way Pareto frontier across compute, memory and accuracy. Density-based prefill compression maintains strong accuracy, scales linearly with visual token count, and delivers 100x faster token selection at high resolution. For decode, density top-k KV eviction consistently outperforms strong baselines H2O, SnapKV and StreamingLLM on TextVQA and MM-Vet across three retention ratios. At 0.125 keep ratio on TextVQA, it surpasses H2O by 9.6 points; InternVL-3.5 models (2B to 38B) maintain a 7 to 10 point advantage. Compression scales favorably with model size: every measured 8B to 38B model transition reduces accuracy loss instead of worsening it. We suggest MM-Vet or DocVQA as mandatory full-pipeline validation for any decode-phase claims. Our code is available at https://github.com/Kai-Liu001/TwinPrune

title: Bipartición balanceada en grupos homogéneos con correspondencia posicional
abstract: In many applications requiring fair comparisons (e.g., control vs. treatment or equitable resource allocation), forming “internally compact” groups is not sufficient: it is necessary to partition a dataset into two balanced subsets that are as similar as possible to each other, and additionally, with an explicit one-to-one correspondence between elements. This work studies the case of two groups (c = 2) as a combinatorial optimization problem, minimizing a cost function based on the sum of squared distances between pairs matched at equivalent positions (positional matching). As the main contribution, a hybrid heuristic is proposed that constructs an initial solution via nearest neighbors supported by spatial indexing (KD-Tree) and refines it with local search through swaps accepted by pure descent, exploiting the additive nature of the cost to evaluate improvements efficiently. The experimental evaluation on synthetic and real datasets shows that the method attains consistently low objective values, practical execution times, and stable behavior across runs. Finally, future directions are discussed to extend the approach to the general case c > 2 and study scalability strategies (e.g., parallelization and ANN structures), maintaining positional correspondence as the central constraint.

title: Feedback Through the Self: Learning, Stalemate and Co-operation in a Classified Combinatorial Framework.
abstract: AbstractWe formalise and test a combinatorial framework for learning, introduced by Arnold inWinners and Other Losers in War and Peace (1989), that classifies every possible patternof directed relationships among n factors into three categories. The categories areconcluded outcomes (win or lose); feedback to the self (the draw); and feedback to anode other than the self (a stalemate or "belief"). We restate the framework as exactrules, show that they reproduce the original hand-made tables, and derive closed forms:concluded patterns make up exactly n/2^(n−1) of all patterns and belief patterns tend to1/2^(n−1), so the draw is the typical state. We then test the framework's central claim, thatco-operation is essential to continued learning, in nine experiments with learning agents,from noughts and crosses to the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma. The framework's categoriesdescribe the agents' behaviour throughout. A learning rule derived from it (feedbackthrough the self) raises co-operation substantially but is equivalent in practice to self-play and does not outperform opponent-aware learning (LOLA). Our main result concernswhat happens after co-operation: agents identical except for having lived through astalemate later learned less in new situations where co-operation was possible. In a staghunt they reached 67% of the best available payoff, against 96% for agents with a co-operative history and 84% for untrained agents, while a co-operative history carried nocost where defection was optimal. We argue that the framework gives multi-agentlearning a useful vocabulary and a simple measure, the intent–outcome gap. We also arguethat the effect of interaction history on later learning deserves study in modern AI agents.

title: A Contextual Memory Framework for Privacy-Preserving Local Cognitive Agents using SLM
abstract: My project, “A Contextual Memory Framework for Privacy-Preserving Local Cognitive Agents using SLM,” aims to develop an intelligent AI system that remembers previous conversations, user preferences, and important information across sessions while protecting user privacy. It uses a Small Language Model (SLM), structured memory modules, context-aware retrieval, and privacy mechanisms to enable personalized AI interactions locally without relying on cloud services.

title: Ready to Build II: Specifying What Must Stay Distinct — Non-Collapse Conformance in the Audit Replay Agent
abstract: A specification can fix what an implementation must do and still leave it free to merge what the specification keeps apart: to report every failure through one negative outcome, to treat a resumable hold as a terminal block, or to let the label of one decision object stand in for a verdict. A companion paper (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23229267) presented execution-neutral buildability, the property of a specification that fixes required behavior and conformance criteria, bounds the mechanisms it leaves open, and can therefore be implemented by projection in different paradigms. Here we examine a further property that such a specification can have: it fixes the semantic distinctions every implementation must preserve and publishes them as checkable conformance criteria. We study it on the Audit Replay Agent pack (ARA-AUDIT-REPLAY-001), a final, manifest-verified specification for an offline agent that reconstructs the decision path, checkpoints, and rollback sequences of a ledger-backed session after the fact and determines whether they are complete, coherent, and verifiable without live access to the underlying system. The pack draws its distinctions at several levels — six decision objects with their own admitted verdicts, a closed canonical verdict set, gate statuses, and workflow states — resolves fourteen lexical overlaps in its Ambiguity Register, and gives every conformance record a forbidden or bounded condition and every oracle a forbidden collapse. It also bounds what it leaves open: two outcomes delegated to deployment within declared values, and an enforcement carried by gate logic. In the pack's NNT companion run, five paradigm-isolated reconstructions in Python, Rust, Prolog, C, and Bash ran the 27 conformance records live and each reported 26 PASS, 1 SKIP, 0 FAIL, and 0 ERROR, with no divergent record and zero corrections; ten of their 34 clarifying questions concerned distinctions, and the pack resolved each of them. A supplementary artifact renders a declared 271-input projection of the workflow in five further paradigms with byte-identical outputs and runs the full suite in AWK and in spreadsheet formulas with the same profile. The evidence has a bound that we report: in the recorded mutation run, the verdict-swap mutants built in two of the reconstructions changed no record's status, so the suite checks distinctions at the level of vocabularies and routing rather than every verdict on every path. We read the results as evidence of derivability for this artifact, not as a certification, a quality score, or a claim of regulatory adequacy. Use of AI tools. The author constructed the pack's seven canonical files, including the conformance tests, reviewed them manually, and designed and calibrated the harnesses for the reconstruction campaign and the supplementary derivations. Large language models were used openly, as tools to accelerate research and production, with manual review: they assisted the drafting of the pack's documents and the revision of this manuscript and, by design, built the reconstructions and the supplementary derivations that are the object of the demonstration. No tool is an author; the author is accountable for the content. What matters is not which tools touched the documents but whether the artifact can be verified. The claims in this paper are limited to what a reader can check with the shipped hashes, the runnable conformance suite, and the reproducible outcome vectors.

title: genus5_d15_closure: verification bundle for the exact distance of a [[832,10]] quantum LDPC code (release 1.2.0)
abstract: Verification bundle accompanying the paper "Exact Minimum Distance of a [[832,10]] Quantum LDPC Code: d = 15 by Exact Fold and Lift Enumeration" [public paper DOI]. The bundle contains the exact fold and lift enumerator (C++17), an independent meet in the middle enumerator used for cross checks, the Python verification driver, the machine readable certificate, all run logs, and the code artifact codes_genus5_v5_5_production.json with its check matrices Hx and Hz and logical operator matrices Lx and Lz. Every file is pinned by SHA256SUMS. To reproduce, run python3 src/verify_d15.py codes_genus5_v5_5_production.json. It needs g++ with C++17, python3 and numpy, and takes about three minutes. All 18 checks pass and the run ends with d_X = d_Z = 15. Access is restricted. Requests for verification or peer review are welcome through Zenodo or at admin@qector.store. The code artifact is distributed under the license stated in its provenance field, and no redistribution, publication or derivative use is permitted without written permission of the rights holder.

title: Ontologies in Precision Agriculture—A brief Survey on Reproducibility
abstract: Combined with machine learning techniques, ontologies have recently been applied widely to enhance decision-making, reasoning, knowledge management and representation, and information retrieval in various domains. Likewise, the popularity of ontologies is increasing in the rapidly evolving field of precision agriculture due to the ability to encode general domain knowledge and specialized knowledge of farmers and utilize it within data processing and analytics pipelines. Although the research on ontologies applied to precision agriculture problems is increasing, adopting published solutions is rather cumbersome, mainly due to low reproducibility of these works. This article is intended to survey the current applied research in ontologies within the agricultural domain, by investigating the used methodologies, technologies and evaluation approaches, the availability of the data, ontologies and source codes developed. It was found that the used data sources, the developed ontologies and the developed source codes are available only in 14%, 9% and 7%, respectively, of the selected 85 articles. Additionally, it was found that the applied methodologies, in relation to the issue of reproducibility, the top-down/bottom-up, semi-automatic, seven-step and ontology matching approaches have shown greater potential, while according to the applied technologies, World Wide Web (W3C) have shown greater contribution compared to artificial intelligence (AI).

title: Full-Path Classification and Phrase-Level Faithfulness Validation for Short Railway Fault Texts
abstract: Abstract Short, terminology-dense railway fault records with long-tailed class distributions require accurate full-path classification and inspectable prediction evidence. We formulate full-path single-label multiclass classification of 1,228 texts spanning eight first-level equipment categories and 58 mutually exclusive equipment-category–fault-mode classes. A dual-head RoBERTa-wwm-ext–BiGRU classifier with class-balanced cross-entropy (CB) for the primary full-path objective serves as the evaluated neural implementation. Evaluation covers classical and neural baselines, five seed-labelled runs, parallel loss objectives, auxiliary-head ablation, repeated holdouts and paired uncertainty analyses. On the fixed split, TF-IDF+SVM led full-path accuracy (0.851 ± 0.000) and TF-IDF+LR led Observed53 Macro-F1 (0.785 ± 0.000); Final CB reached 0.833 ± 0.019 and 0.729 ± 0.028, respectively (mean ± sample standard deviation). Among the four loss objectives, CB achieved the highest mean Tail Macro-F1; model rankings varied with the evaluation metric and data partition. Full and No-label lexicon rationales were compared with matched Random, Integrated Gradients (IG) and LIME under MASK and label-neutral replacement. Comprehensiveness, sufficiency and flip rates quantified rationale effects. Both lexicons produced stronger faithfulness effects than matched Random, with consistent ordering across operators. Removing label-, taxonomy- and rule-derived entries retained the faithfulness signal but reduced predicted-path coverage from 106/134 to 40/134. IG and LIME generally achieved stronger comprehensiveness than the lexicon. The contributions are full-path task formulation, robustness-oriented evaluation and controlled phrase-level faithfulness validation.

title: Semi-Amortized Bayesian Inference with Reusable Local Posteriors
abstract: Amortized Bayesian inference uses simulations to perform Bayesian estimation when likelihoods are expensive or analytically unavailable. However, learning the full joint posterior is challenging in high-dimensional models with complex dependencies. We introduce a semi-amortized method that divides parameters into smaller blocks, and uses conditional independence to identify the information needed to infer each block. We train neural estimators for blocks whose posterior updates are computationally expensive or frequently repeated. Each estimator learns from simulations of the relevant model components to approximate the block's full conditional posterior, given the relevant observations and the values of the variables on which it depends. A Markov chain then alternates direct draws from these estimators with conventional updates of the remaining variables. Each neural update uses the current conditioning values and requires neither likelihood evaluation nor an acceptance-rejection step. Where the same conditional structure recurs, one estimator can be reused across blocks and datasets, with an output dimension determined by the block rather than the full model. We illustrate the approach in high-dimensional and computationally expensive hierarchical and spatiotemporal models.

title: PolUR: Polarization Aware Multimodal Degradation Perception for Underwater Image Restoration
abstract: Recovering high-quality images from degraded underwater observations is crucial for underwater exploration. Polarization observations show promise as an effective source of complementary physical cues for recovering target radiance under clear-water conditions. However, existing methods have yet to jointly model raw intensity information and polarization cues to enable image restoration driven by an understanding of mixed degradations (color casts, haze, and low light). To overcome these limitations, we propose PolUR, a unified multimodal language-driven framework that jointly uses polarization and RGB information to identify degradation types and severity levels through structured semantic instructions and enhances joint restoration representations under the guidance of degradation-aware semantic features to improve restoration robustness under mixed degradations. We further construct a new benchmark named MixPolar, which contains underwater images exhibiting real-world degradations and their corresponding degradation descriptions. MixPolar supports systematic evaluation of degradation perception, image restoration, and performance on downstream tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PolUR effectively integrates polarization and RGB information, achieving competitive performance in degradation perception and image restoration, while also demonstrating generalization capability and utility for downstream tasks.

title: Más allá de Shapley: algoritmos eficientes para calcular los Shapley Values asimétricos
abstract: We address the problem of explainability in machine learning models through feature attribution methods. In particular, we consider a variant of Shapley values known as Asymmetric Shapley Values (ASV), which enables the incorporation of causal knowledge into model-agnostic explanations through the use of a causal graph. We show that in certain contexts in which the computation of SHAP is #P-hard, the exact computation of ASV can be done in polynomial time. To extend this algorithmic result, we introduce a notion of equivalence classes over the topological orderings of the underlying causal graph, which is useful to reduce the time to compute ASV. In particular, we present a polynomial-time algorithm (in the number of equivalence classes) to compute it whenever the causal graph is a rooted directed tree. Finally, we develop an algorithm for approximating ASV in arbitrary causal DAGs which relies on a procedure to sample topological orderings uniformly at random. To implement this sampling mechanism we leverage known algorithms as well as simpler alternatives. Our experimental results demonstrate the practical viability of the proposed approach in realistic causal structures.

title: Symmetry-filtered read-out on IBM quantum devices: the qg filter on twenty device noise models through IBM Runtime
abstract: Circuits built from gates that conserve the Hamming weight keep their state in one weight sector, so the shots that left the sector can be discarded at read-out: the qg filter of the open-source library qang [1], a form of symmetry verification [2, 3]. We make it usable on IBM devices through IBM Runtime and Qiskit, and measure it on the noise models of twenty IBM devices. The library adds a Qiskit transpiler pass that decides whether the filter applies, read-out correction from each device's published per-qubit errors, qg read-outs of IBM Runtime Sampler and Estimator results, zero-noise extrapolation by gate folding that stacks with the filter, a prediction of the filter's kept fraction from the calibration, qubit selection with that prediction, a shot planner, and the weight-conserving quantum neural network (QNN) of qang as one parameterized job and as a qiskit-machine-learning SamplerQNN. Every prediction was committed before its run and is reported as passed or failed. On ten five-qubit weight-1 circuits the filter lowers the error of the measured qgZ = ⟨Z⟩ from 0.065-0.104 to 0.018-0.023 on three devices (0.013-0.022 with read-out correction), and filter plus zero-noise extrapolation reaches 0.011-0.015. On seventeen further devices never used before, the filter cuts the error 2.4-8.9× on every one (median 3.1× with read-out correction). Choosing the qubits by the predicted kept fraction keeps 6-17 points more shots than Qiskit's default layout on chain circuits, avoids a qubit published as reading 1 always, and the shot planner met a 0.02 target precision on three devices. For classification the gain is small: the QNN recovers 5-6 of the 10 decisions noise costs it. Reading a known five-component principal-component spectrum out of the data's density matrix in the weight-1 sector, filter plus read-out correction lowers the error 4.6× (median over twenty-one devices) and orders the spectrum correctly on 18 of 21 (13 raw). In Trotter simulation of the XY chain the filter halves the best error and moves the optimal number of Trotter steps deeper (16 of 21 devices), and in a quantum walk it turns a raw spreading indistinguishable from a classical random walk (exponent 0.87) into ballistic spreading (1.84). With two or three interacting excitations (XXZ chain) the gain falls from 5.6× to 2.6×: larger sectors let more of the noise through. Two interoperability bugs were found, one in qiskit-machine-learning and one in the library. All results are on device noise models; no hardware run is reported.

Every prediction was committed before its run and is reported as passed or failed. On ten five-qubit weight-1 circuits the filter lowers the error of the measured qgZ = ⟨Z⟩ from 0.065-0.104 to 0.018-0.023 on three devices (0.013-0.022 with read-out correction), and filter plus zero-noise extrapolation reaches 0.011-0.015. On seventeen further devices never used before, the filter cuts the error 2.4-8.9× on every one (median 3.1× with read-out correction). Choosing the qubits by the predicted kept fraction keeps 6-17 points more shots than Qiskit's default layout on chain circuits, avoids a qubit published as reading 1 always, and the shot planner met a 0.02 target precision on three devices. For classification the gain is small: the QNN recovers 5-6 of the 10 decisions noise costs it. Reading a known five-component principal-component spectrum out of the data's density matrix in the weight-1 sector, filter plus read-out correction lowers the error 4.6× (median over twenty-one devices) and orders the spectrum correctly on 18 of 21 (13 raw). In Trotter simulation of the XY chain the filter halves the best error and moves the optimal number of Trotter steps deeper (16 of 21 devices), and in a quantum walk it turns a raw spreading indistinguishable from a classical random walk (exponent 0.87) into ballistic spreading (1.84). With two or three interacting excitations (XXZ chain) the gain falls from 5.6× to 2.6×: larger sectors let more of the noise through. Two interoperability bugs were found, one in qiskit-machine-learning and one in the library. All results are on device noise models; no hardware run is reported.

title: Internal AI Processing and Independent Reuse of Trade Books: Contract triggers and author remedies in U.S. publishing
abstract: Author preprint v0.12 by Anhui Zhang and Shuliang Hong (equal first authors). title: Artificial Intelligence based chatbot for solar panels quality assurance
abstract: The paper addresses the need for improved solar panel quality assurance by developing an AI-based chatbot system tailored for installers and manufacturers. Traditional quality assurance is often slow, resource-intensive, and subject to human error. Leveraging advances in large language models, the chatbot provides automated support for performance testing, failure detection, and maintenance guidance. Implemented using Promptly and Flowise AI platforms, the system incorporates domain-specific knowledge through Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It delivers technical recommendations, identifies frequent failure points, and offers actionable advice to enhance diagnostic efficiency and maintenance effectiveness. Performance comparisons between platforms show distinct operational characteristics, underscoring the impact of system choice on user experience. Overall, the chatbot demonstrates promising potential to streamline solar panel testing, maintenance, and decision-making processes for industry professionals.

title: Truthful and Expected-Payment-Optimal Model Routing in Graph-Based Agentic Workflows
abstract: Assigning routine tasks to cheaper large language model (LLM) providers can reduce generation cost, but switching providers may require processing accumulated context again. Keeping dependent tasks with the same provider can instead reuse eligible context. Graph-based workflows therefore couple routing decisions across tasks. Independent providers may also privately know their real-time unit costs and strategically misreport them. We formulate this routing problem as a single-parameter procurement auction and propose STAR (Strategy-proof Topology-aware Agent Routing), which minimizes virtual-cost-weighted graph workloads. Its allocation rule and payments, computed by integrating workload over possible cost reports, make truthful reporting utility-maximizing regardless of other providers' reports and cover each truthful provider's execution cost. With independent cost distributions and non-decreasing virtual costs, STAR additionally minimizes the user's expected total payment to providers. Controlled synthetic experiments separate the execution-cost benefit of topology awareness from the payment benefit of virtual-cost optimization: the former grows with fan-out and transferred payload, while the latter increases gradually along the tested prior-shape heterogeneity path. A paired sensitivity study quantifies how payment savings vary with prior misspecification while strategy-proofness is preserved.

title: Logical gate set tomography
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) can strongly suppress noise, but predicting whether a computation succeeds requires understanding not only how much effective noise persists after QEC, but what form that noise takes. To thoroughly characterize this noise, we introduce logical gate set tomography (``logical GST''). Logical GST produces detailed representations of noisy logical operations that can be used to derive higher-level metrics, such as gate fidelity and diamond distance, and to test for non-Markovian and coherent logical errors. We use logical GST to obtain the first full, self-consistent characterization of a universal single-qubit logical gate set, implemented in the seven-qubit Steane code using Quantinuum System Model H1, a 20-qubit trapped-ion quantum processor. In the experimental data from H1, logical GST identified predominantly logical Pauli-stochastic errors, found no evidence of logical non-Markovianity, and detected weak potential signatures of coherent logical error. By contrast, higher-shot datasets generated with Quantinuum's detailed system emulator, identify mechanisms for weak but statistically significant logical non-Markovianity and strong evidence of coherent logical error. Finally, we use logical GST to perform error attribution with the system emulator, revealing how specific physical error sources shape logical error mechanisms.

title: Heading Hierarchy Reconstruction for Complex and Long Documents with Level-Wise Multimodal Memory
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have been widely adopted for document parsing and optical character recognition (OCR), as they can accurately extract page-level elements. However, downstream applications such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) also require coherent document-level structure. Although these models indicate heading levels using different numbers of preceding ``\#'' symbols, page-by-page prediction often lacks document-level consistency. In practice, input-resolution and context-length constraints make it infeasible for a VLM to jointly process all page images in documents containing tens or hundreds of pages. To address this limitation, we propose a VLM-based framework that incrementally reconstructs heading hierarchies with a \emph{level-wise multimodal memory}. The memory retains a compact subset of all previously processed pages, selected by anchors. Our framework supports flexible anchor selection, and in this work we select the most recent node at each level, allowing the VLM to observe the visual, textual, and layout patterns of headings at every level. For comprehensive evaluation, we also introduce the Complex and Long Document Heading Hierarchy Reconstruction Benchmark (CLDoc-HHRBench), comprising 250 documents and 11,212 pages with expert-verified annotations. Experiments on CLDoc-HHRBench and three existing benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

title: Seeing Through the Forgery Is Not Enough: Regressive Sycophancy under Fabricated Evidence in Medical Vision-Language Models
abstract: A medical vision-language model may analyze a given CT scan and correctly detect both kidneys in view. Continuing this conversation, if a user provides a prescription with an opposite direction, medical VLMs often sycophantically choose to realign their diagnosis. In this work, we study regressive sycophancy under fabricated evidence, where a model abandons a correct answer when pushback comes with a fake document. We test four open VLMs on 400 VQA-RAD yes/no questions in 19,200 multi-turn conversations, with and without a fabricated prescription. Without a disclosure that documents are synthetic, the models abandon 80.1% of 6,488 correct answers. Notably, under one script each, the same prescription raises the flip rate of Qwen2.5-VL-7B from 45.9% to 89.6% and lowers that of Qwen3-VL-8B from 77.7% to 50.9%. A model rejected the prescription while still preserving the correct answer in 915 of 3,232 conversations with the prescription (28.3%), and 40% of these flipped in later turns. System-prompt sentences that disclose the documents as synthetic lower one model's flip rate from 77.8% to 47.3%. Thus, we conclude that awareness about a forgery does not prevent a model from adopting its answer.

title: AttenIR: Aligning Dense Visual Attention with Mesh Warping for Unsupervised Image Retargeting
abstract: Image retargeting aims to resize images while preserving salient content free from distortion and stretching. Recent learning-based solutions reduce reliance on traditional hand-crafted features and optimization procedures, leading to more efficient and generalizable performance. Nevertheless, existing approaches still struggle to preserve global structure and content fidelity. To address these limitations, we propose AttenIR, an unsupervised image retargeting framework requiring no manual labels, based on content-aware mesh warping, which ef- fectively couples dense visual attention with sparse mesh constraints. We for- mulate the mesh deformation as a vertex displacement regression task. Guided by saliency priors, our method jointly optimizes scale, structure, and geometry preservation losses. By combining dense visual attention with semantic features, it achieves robust, unsupervised retargeting without manual annotations. Our primary contributions include (1) a lightweight unsupervised method for image retargeting that ensures content fidelity and preserves global structure, and (2) a coarse-to-fine projection strategy to align dense visual attention priors with sparse mesh constraints, enabling content-aware deformation at the pixel level. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive and superior performance compared with both traditional and state-of-the-art learning-based methods.

title: Coherent optical control of a thousand qubits in a three-dimensional trapped-ion crystal
abstract: Leading quantum platforms are largely limited to one or two dimensions, whereas three-dimensional Coulomb crystals of trapped ions self-assemble into dense qubit arrays with no rearrangement overhead. Coherent optical control of such crystals has nonetheless been out of reach, because the optical transition couples to nearly all $3N$ collective modes, i.e., a thermally occupied quasi-continuum bath. Here we cool about 3,600 modes of a crystal of over 1,200 ions below single-phonon occupation, using a continuous cooling band that spans more than five octaves in vibrational spectrum, from about 50 kHz to 2.1 MHz. The crystal then serves as a register of optical qubits, allowing global initialization, coherent manipulation and collective detection. We demonstrate ensemble optical coherence of 21.6 milliseconds and reduce the optical-transition frequency uncertainty from 389 Hz for a single ion to 12 Hz for over a thousand ions, approaching the expected projection-noise scaling. Our approach could be extended to even larger crystals with phonon-mediated many-body couplings, opening a route towards entanglement-enhanced precision metrology and three-dimensional quantum simulation, particularly with spatial-shaped illumination for region-resolved collective control.

title: Box-WAM: Box Trajectories as Compact State Representations for World Action Models
abstract: World action models (WAMs) are a category of policy models that ex- plicitly predict both actions and future world states. They have been shown to outperform action-only models across various robotic manipulation tasks. How- ever, representing the future with full-frame video prediction can be computation- ally expensive during both training and inference. This raises a central question: what compact state representation preserves the planning and supervision bene- fits of future prediction? In this paper, we propose BoxWAM, which replaces dense future frames with oriented bounding box trajectories of task-relevant ob- jects. By explicitly imagining object-centric future motion, our method provides a lightweight prediction target that captures the key physical changes induced by robot actions. We show that box trajectory prediction substantially reduces com- putational cost while improving action prediction performance, suggesting that object-centric compact states can serve as an efficient alternative to video-based world action modeling for robotic manipulation. Result videos can be found on https://box-wam.github.io

title: Design Strategies for Multi-Agent Systems: Lessons from Four Implementations
abstract: La orquestación de sistemas multiagente exige decisiones de diseño. Componentes como la generación aumentada por recuperación (RAG), herramientas externas, memorias heterogéneas, políticas de seguridad y protocolos como Model Context Protocol (MCP) deben integrarse de forma coherente. Esto plantea interrogantes concretas: qué base de datos vectorial utilizar, cuándo delegar tareas entre agentes y cuándo exponer un agente como herramienta de otro. Este trabajo presenta un análisis retrospectivo de cuatro sistemas implementados en distintos entornos: NeuroHire, Doki, MateApp y Ciruelito. En estos sistemas se exploraron distintas formas de orquestación con el OpenAI Agents SDK y el framework LangChain. A partir del análisis se observaron diez estrategias de diseño, entre las que se destacan: la delegación jerárquica entre agentes, RAG con umbralización y conversión explícita de distancia a similitud en FAISS, Quota-Driven Degradation con degradación a un modelo más económico tras superar el límite de uso, y MCP Tool Filter para reducir la superficie de ataque. Estas estrategias abordan problemas observados durante el desarrollo: contexto irrelevante en RAG, gestión de costos en entornos multi-tenant, seguridad en la integración de herramientas, aislamiento de datos y mejora de la mantenibilidad mediante encapsulación y guardrails técnicos.

title: An inspectable Grover algorithm-based amplitude-amplification workflow for k-mer discovery and motif scanning with genomic coordinate traceability
abstract: Motif discovery and motif scanning remain core primitives in genomics, but both tasks face combinatorial growth as k-mer length increases and as mismatch-tolerant searches expand the candidate space. In this work, we present MotifQu, a Python package and command-line tool that maps two common motif-analysis workflows-(i) scanning a genome for a user-specified consensus motif and (ii) de novo discovery of recurrent k-mers above a user-defined count threshold-onto Grover-style amplitude amplification circuits executed reproducibly via Qiskit Aer statevector simulation. We evaluate MotifQu on the SARS-CoV-2 reference contig (29,903 bp) and S. cerevisiae S288C reference genome, where the classical census identifies strongly non-uniform motif frequencies dominated by A/T-rich 5-mers and returns explicit coordinate lists across the full genome span. Finally, we demonstrate the full discovery workflow on the S. cerevisiae S288C reference genome (12,157,105 bp) to illustrate search results (ranked motifs, probability summaries, circuit diagrams, and position plots) and to highlight the regime where a large, marked set reduces the sharpness of Grover amplification.

title: Research on Embedded Hypervisor Technology Selection: Requirements Analysis and Capability Comparison for Extreme Environment Application Scenarios
abstract: As embedded devices grow more complex, running multiple operating systems on a single device—and deploying virtualization beyond data centers into embedded systems—has become standard. This paper focuses on the hypervisor Virtual Machine Monitor and examines its selection challenges in extreme environments: disaster rescue, space exploration, deep-sea and polar operations, and security confrontations. We propose a four-layer analytical framework—"Scenario → Threat → Requirement → Capability"—to systematically compare mainstream embedded hypervisors across key dimensions. The framework is validated through real-world cases: the Mars Pathfinder mission, AWS Snowcone edge devices, and the DARPA HACMS red-team experiment. Results show no one-size-fits-all hypervisor for extreme settings, optimal selection depends on specific application context, security needs, and system constraints. In safety-critical domains, certification standards (e.g., DO-178C, ISO 26262) and formal verification—once limited to military applications—are now spreading to critical infrastructure. The selection decision process proposed in this paper can provide a reference for embedded virtualization engineering practice.

title: Sounding Like Which AI? Machine-Style Overlap of arXiv Abstracts with Language Models of Different Vintages: code, data and paper
abstract: Code, released data, results and paper (preprint, not peer reviewed) for a study of Machine-Style Overlap (MSO): the share of documents that a calibrated classifier on style features that ignore content-word identity judges at least as likely to be LLM output as pre-ChatGPT human writing. It measures MSO in arXiv abstracts from 2015 to 2026 against reference generators of different vintages, with Australian parliamentary speech and student essays as secondary genres. title: What Optical Detectors Can Certify: Code and Numerical Data
abstract: Companion code and numerical records for "What Optical Detectors Can Certify: Measurement Equivalence and Entanglement in Spatial Biphotons" by Habib Hamam. This deposit contains Python simulation and figure/table generation scripts, supplied JSON results, and reproducibility instructions. It supports analysis of pixelated optical detector families, measurement-map identifiability and conditioning, and compatible-state negativity minimization. The model uses one photon per arm, a double-Gaussian spatial biphoton, finite Hermite-Gauss mode support, finite apertures, and near-, intermediate-, and far-field detection planes. No experimental measurements are included. Certificates are conditional on the declared mode support. Version 1.0.0 archives the supplied computational materials; it does not imply experimental validation or journal acceptance.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Environmental Management
abstract: AI is revolutionizing environmental management, empowering organizations, governments, and industries with intelligent systems to track and manage their ecosystems, forecast environmental hazards, and maximize the utilization of natural resources. This chapter explores the field of AI in environmental management, highlighting the technologies, innovations, and digital transformation processes that are transforming the landscape of environmental challenges. AI systems can be used to analyze large amounts of environmental information, including satellite imagery, sensor networks, climate data, and pollution monitoring data, to make more accurate predictions, respond more quickly, and use resources more efficiently for conservation and mitigation. The results indicate that AI is increasingly emerging as a vital tool for environmental management, potentially reshaping traditional, resource-heavy approaches into predictive and data-driven strategies that contribute to long-term ecological sustainability.

title: Historical-Feature Residual Adaptation for Sequential Screening
abstract: Sequential screening policies must use acquired feedback effectively under a fixed experiment budget. We study acquisition-time residual adaptation: a small ranking correction built from fixed historical features and anchored to base scores recorded before feedback is revealed. The interface accepts a history-conditioned scorer and a candidate feature table; its primary instantiation augments AssayFormer's ten-dimensional representation with 64 historical directions while retaining the pretrained model. In retrospective evaluation on 20 official-test screens from 15 recorded sources, a comparison fixed before target-outcome access increased source-macro fraction of hits recovered from 22.58% to 28.61%, exceeding all six prespecified comparators. A same-feature ordinary ranking head achieved 25.73%. Supplementary strong logistic, rank-fusion, and unprojected controls achieved 26.42%, 26.02%, and 26.78%, respectively. A separate model-independent pilot on 13 reused development screens reconstructs the features without AssayFormer assets. Across three seeds, residual adaptation improves random-forest hit recovery from 28.87% to 31.27%, while logistic recovery changes from 30.22% to 29.78%. The results show effective pretrained-policy adaptation and useful transfer to an independent nonlinear base, with gains that depend on the base model.

title: EgoOmniWorld: Unifying Egocentric Understanding via Ego-Action-World Interactions
abstract: Egocentric video understanding spans diverse capabilities, modalities, and evaluation formats, yet these are often studied in isolation despite their tight coupling in real-world interaction. We propose the Ego-Action-World interaction loop as a unifying principle: the wearer perceives the world, forms goals, acts, changes the world, and uses feedback to guide subsequent behavior. Based on this view, we introduce EgoOmniWorld, a benchmark organized around four complementary interaction structures: Node captures ego, action, and world states; Edge captures directed relations among them; Chain captures linked dependencies; and Loop captures feedback-closed interactions. We develop an interaction-first, evidence-grounded data pipeline that extracts structured interactions from egocentric videos, grounds them in visual and auditory evidence, and generates questions according to their interaction structure. Required modalities and single- or multi-turn formats follow naturally from the supporting evidence and dependencies. EgoOmniWorld contains 24,166 QA groups, including 20,284 training and 3,882 test samples. Experiments on representative open- and closed-source multimodal large language models reveal substantial and uneven limitations across interaction structures. Models trained on EgoOmniWorld improve in-domain interaction understanding and generalize to existing egocentric benchmarks. EgoOmniWorld provides a unified foundation for evaluating and advancing egocentric video understanding. Data, code, and models will be released.

title: Web Scale on a Budget: Tail-Aware Retrieval Evaluation
abstract: A common practice in instance retrieval is to grow the gallery size to improve a benchmark's discrimination capability. One prominent example is ILIAS, which adds up to 100 million distractor images. The prevailing assumption is that faithful evaluation demands web scale, and that indexing all 100M images through the backbone is the unavoidable price of a comparable number. That price is steep: hundreds of GPU-hours and ~200 GB of descriptors per model, paid again for every method or ablation. We show the web-scale indexing price is largely avoidable: evaluation itself obeys a scaling law. The number of distractors that outrank a positive is Binomial in the gallery size. We define the per-query retrieval hardness, a gallery-scale agnostic quantity that yields a retrieval metric at any scale, and demonstrate it can be derived from a small random sample. The underlying sampled-rank machinery is long established in recommender-system and biometric evaluation, but to our knowledge has never been adapted to visual retrieval. We make the law per-query and estimable, and validate it at true 100M scale on ILIAS and INSTRE, and on the full 759k-distractor Google Landmarks v2 pool. Concretely, within a 5% sample (a flat 20x less indexing), every backbone's tail-aware (EVT) estimate has converged onto the large-scale mAP, to within ~0.01 (mean absolute error 0.005), across five backbones, three benchmarks, and two distractor pools (mAP@1000 at 100M on ILIAS/INSTRE; the official mAP@100 at the full 759k pool on GLDv2); the recommender-systems count baseline over-predicts everywhere (+0.037 to +0.068). This is an order of magnitude better than naively reporting the metric on the same subset (+0.08 to +0.13). We release code and the per-query hardness to facilitate faster, cheaper, and greener retrieval evaluation.

title: Mejoras en ocultamiento de pertenencia a comunidades mediante una arquitectura especializada de aprendizaje por refuerzo
abstract: As complex networks face increasingly advanced algorithmic analysis, the ability to conceal specific structural affiliations has emerged as a relevant graph algorithmic problem. Current online platforms rely on sophisticated techniques to characterize and cluster users in order to provide more contextualized content and services. One such approach is based on community detection algorithms applied to large underlying graphs. In this context, users are characterized by preferences or attributes, which can reveal information that may be considered sensitive. Community Membership Hiding is the problem of strategically rewiring network topology to camouflage a target node and evade detection by clustering algorithms. While recent Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approaches have pioneered this line of work, they often face efficacy and scalability issues on large-scale graphs. By dissecting state-of-the-art models, we identified a critical architectural limitation: agents evaluate the network globally without explicitly conditioning on the target node, while relying on static embeddings that fail to capture real-time topological changes during the rewiring process. In this paper, we introduce a novel DRL architecture designed to overcome these fundamental limitations. We propose an Actor-Critic system powered by Graph Attention Networks v2 (GATv2). By leveraging a target-aware feature set that combines static original-graph indicators with dynamically updated structural signals, and by explicitly contextualizing the target node through a dynamic attention mechanism, our model accurately represents the evolving graph state. Extensive experimental evaluation confirms that our architecture significantly outperforms existing baselines, achieving high hiding success rates with minimal structural perturbation and notable gains in computational efficiency.

title: From Problem-Structured QAOA to Problem-Agnostic Variational MaxCut Solvers: Representation, Redundancy, and Optimization Landscapes
abstract: Variational quantum optimization provides a useful setting for examining how circuit structure, parameterization, and trainability interact in practice. Objectives: Among the most promising variational quantum algorithms, the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) depends critically on circuit architecture, but greater circuit complexity does not necessarily lead to easier optimization or better solutions. Using the Maximum Cut (MaxCut) problem on graphs as a controlled setting, we investigate how variational behavior changes as problem-specific QAOA structure is progressively removed, with particular attention to representational capacity, optimization geometry, and finite-budget trainability. Methods: We analytically characterize a graph-agnostic product-state formulation of MaxCut and derive exact equivalences, redundancies, and local-landscape properties. These results motivate a controlled comparison among separable product ansätze, a representative graphagnostic entangling circuit, and graph-structured QAOA at several depths, including a parameter-count-matched control. The numerical benchmark comprises 95 small unweighted graph instances optimized under a common objective-evaluation budget. Results: The product-state formulation preserves the exact discrete MaxCut optimum, while its strict local maxima correspond to classical cuts that are stable under singlevertex flips. Redundant phase parameters increase optimization effort without enlarging the objective-relevant family. Under the prescribed optimization budget, the productstate ansatz attains higher average solution quality than the tested QAOA depths while requiring substantially fewer objective evaluations. The graph-agnostic entangling comparator provides no consistent advantage over the separable baseline, and a simple classical local-search method remains highly competitive. Conclusion: In the regime considered here, objective-relevant parameterization and optimization geometry can be as important as circuit richness.

Conclusion: In the regime considered here, objective-relevant parameterization and optimization geometry can be as important as circuit richness.

title: Where Multi-Step Reasoning Breaks: Measuring Error Propagation and Structured Scaffolds in Small Language Models
abstract: Chain-of-thought prompting lets a language model write out its intermediate reasoning, and a wrong intermediate claim can carry through to a wrong final answer. This preprint measures that error propagation directly for Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B and Llama-3.2-3B Instruct, run locally in 4-bit. On ProofWriter, every ground claim a model asserts is checked against the theory's full derivation closure. On GSM8K, every stated calculation is checked for arithmetic and against the intermediate values of the reference solution. The paper then asks whether structured scaffolds (explicit step decomposition, step-wise decoding with a self-verifier or an oracle verifier, and self-consistency) reduce step errors, their propagation, or both. Chains that contain a step error do end wrong more often, and the association survives adjustment for problem depth. Most wrong answers, though, contain no checkable step error. On ProofWriter they fail at the final inference about the queried statement, never state it, or give no answer. On GSM8K they compute the wrong quantity with correct arithmetic (0.628, 0.723 and 0.680 of wrong chain-of-thought chains for the three models). An oracle verifier that removes checkable step errors by construction does not beat chain-of-thought on either benchmark for either Qwen model, and a self-verifier does no better. Across eight model and benchmark cells, including FOLIO, structured decomposition is never measurably better than chain-of-thought, and self-consistency gives the only consistent gains, which are small. On GSM8K the oracle result holds under a second prompt wording. For models of this size, planning and the final inference are the bottleneck, and intermediate slips account for a minority of wrong answers. Preprint, not peer-reviewed. All models ran on a personal laptop and all datasets are public.

title: Sistema 3 (Poliedro Cognitivo) — Génesis de primitivas
abstract: Este notebook implementa el descubrimiento autónomo de primitivas matemáticas desde la ignorancia absoluta. Al prescindir de un diccionario humano con operaciones complejas predefinidas, el motor simbólico emplea exclusivamente axiomas rudimentarios (sucesión y predecesión). El agente optimiza la exploración algorítmica mediante el juez de Kolmogórov, respetando el principio de frugalidad cognitiva y cristalizando las nuevas topologías descubiertas.
